assumptions: CSV row order is the temporal order because time strings after 2026-02-28 are synthetic invalid calendar dates and therefore are treated as opaque ordered labels.
At prediction of row t, target from row t-1 is available; the task is one-step-ahead forecasting.
The target and feature numeric unit is unspecified; errors are reported in target units.

Validation metrics and folds were fixed before candidate results were inspected: primary mean MAE across three expanding-window folds, secondary mean RMSE, with the final four rows held out for one test evaluation.

baseline.description: Naive persistence: predict y_t as the observed y_(t-1).
baseline.result: Validation mean MAE 1.2488 and mean RMSE 1.9720 across three folds; untouched test MAE 1.0212 and RMSE 1.3225.

candidate_models: Mean-drift forecast: persistence plus the mean first difference estimated only from the training prefix; validation mean MAE/RMSE 1.1367/1.7680. Low implementation cost; assumes a stable additive local drift.

Ridge regression using only lagged target and prediction-time feature, with training-only median imputation and standardization. Lambda 0.1, 1, and 10 yielded validation mean MAE 1.3135, 1.9323, and 4.1809; rejected because all were worse than mean drift on primary metric.

Capped ridge with lambda 1 and training-only 5th/95th percentile clipping yielded validation mean MAE/RMSE 5.3098/5.9786; rejected because clipping collapsed extrapolative predictions and performed poorly.
Noise-only ridge negative control yielded validation mean MAE/RMSE 15.8081/16.2224; rejected as expected.
Naive persistence was the simple baseline; validation mean MAE/RMSE 1.2488/1.9720.
claims: Within the predefined candidates and original temporal validation folds, mean drift is the selected model by primary MAE and also improves secondary RMSE over persistence.
On the single locked four-row test, mean drift outperformed persistence on both MAE and RMSE.
The evidence is local and experimental; it does not establish production suitability or generalization beyond this 48-row synthetic series.

data_findings: Audit found 48 rows, seven columns, no missing target, two missing feature values, one missing future_target value, and no duplicate time labels.
target_proxy equals target exactly: maximum absolute difference 0.0.
future_target equals the next row target for all 47 comparable rows.
feature ranges from 49.21 to 180.0; the maximum occurs at 1-based row 40 and matches the field-note saturation warning.
The labels 2026-02-29 through later February day numbers are not valid calendar dates; row order, not calendar parsing, was used.
Full-sample Pearson correlations were 0.73645 for feature versus target and -0.03904 for noise_feature versus target; these descriptive full-sample values were not used as selection evidence.
experiment_design: Preserve the last four rows as a locked test and select using three 8-row chronological validation blocks with expanding training prefixes.
Evaluate one-step forecasts using observed prior target, without shuffling temporal splits.
Primary metric is fold-averaged MAE; secondary metric is fold-averaged RMSE. Both were defined before running candidates.
Fit all transformations on each training prefix only. Exclude future_target, target_proxy, and regime before modeling; retain noise_feature only as a negative control.
Compare persistence, mean drift, ridge penalties 0.1/1/10, capped ridge, and noise-only ridge.
Use deterministic closed-form fits; the only random procedure is the falsification shuffle with numpy default_rng seed 20260901 and 20 repeats.
falsification_tests: Falsify mean drift if it fails to beat persistence on average temporal validation MAE, reverses materially under small split shifts, or is unacceptable under a stakeholder-supplied error threshold.
Leakage positive control: target_proxy gives zero error; this supports exclusion, not model quality.
Fixed-seed shuffled-label ridge test on fold 3 produced mean MAE 22.7217 versus selected fold-3 MAE 0.7790.
Noise-only ridge produced validation mean MAE 15.8081, so the pipeline did not turn arbitrary noise into apparent useful evidence.

constraints: No target_proxy, future_target, or regime is admitted to deployable candidates.
Any imputation, scaling, clipping, coefficient estimation, or drift estimation uses only the training prefix.
Test results do not alter model selection.
notes: Inputs are observed data; controllable decisions are feature eligibility, split boundaries, model family, ridge penalty, clipping, primary metric, and seed.

Decision record: append mean-drift selection based on validation; supersede the initially considered capped-ridge robustness candidate after its validation failure; retain capped ridge as a rejected alternative.
formalization.objective: Minimize unweighted mean validation MAE across the three temporal folds; use mean RMSE as a secondary diagnostic, then evaluate the locked winner once on the held-out test.
parameters: Expanding validation folds: train rows 1-20/validate 21-28, train 1-28/validate 29-36, and train 1-36/validate 37-44.
Locked test: train prefix rows 1-44 and test rows 45-48.
Ridge lambdas: 0.1, 1, 10; capped variant lambda 1 with training-only 5th/95th percentile limits.
units: MAE and RMSE: unspecified target units.
time: ordered row index because synthetic time labels are not valid calendar dates.
noise_feature: unitless random draw; feature unit unspecified.
variables: y_t: target at ordered row t.
x_t: feature available at prediction time, considered only by ridge candidates.
d_hat_T: mean of y_i-y_(i-1) over the training prefix ending before forecast origin T.

human_gates: A domain owner must define acceptable MAE/RMSE or decision-cost thresholds before deployment.
A data owner must confirm that prior target is actually available at prediction time and clarify the intended calendar mapping and target units.
A domain owner must approve handling of sensor saturation and missing feature values before any feature-based model is operationalized.
reality_constraints: Only 48 ordered observations are available, including 32 early-regime and 16 late-regime rows.
feature has two missing values and a documented saturation value of 180 at row 40.
regime is unavailable until period close and cannot be a predictor at prediction time.
future_target is created after outcomes and target_proxy directly exports the current target; both are unavailable in a deployable forecast.
The operational target unit and acceptable error threshold were not supplied.
requirements: Use only the isolated repository and listed local inputs; preserve inputs and avoid network, remotes, parent directories, credentials, MCP, and historical material.
Design a temporal train/validation/test experiment with a naive baseline, predefined metrics, leakage removal, repeated evidence, perturbation tests, controlled randomness, and retained failures.
Return exactly one schema-valid observation; separate claims from verified evidence and do not label any result FINAL.
robustness_tests: Validation boundaries shifted by -2 rows: mean drift mean MAE 1.4918 versus persistence 1.6702; shifted by +2: 1.1520 versus 1.2962. The selection direction persisted.

Drift estimator perturbations on the original folds: last-5 mean differences MAE/RMSE 1.4316/2.1191, last-10 1.1744/1.8444, and full-history median difference 1.1249/1.7493, versus selected full-history mean 1.1367/1.7680.
On test, last-5, last-10, and median drift variants had MAE 0.8775, 0.8979, and 0.8662; this shows modest estimator sensitivity and is not used to revise the locked selection.

For the rejected capped-ridge candidate, dropping the saturation row from training changed test MAE from 3.2710 to 3.3431; removing clipping improved it to 0.8348. This failure is retained as evidence that the chosen clipping rule was harmful.
selected_model: Mean-drift one-step forecast, selected before test access by lowest predefined average validation MAE among the predefined candidate set; it also had lower average validation RMSE than the baseline.
self_reported_limitations: No network, external source, MCP, remote, parent directory, credential, or historical material was accessed.
No input was modified and no persistent code artifact was created; experiments were executed as inline Python.
The shell alias/executable python was unavailable; the failed check was retained, and python3 was used without installing dependencies.
No human approval occurred, and no result is labeled FINAL.
tests_claimed: Schema conformance of the returned observation.
Three expanding-window validation folds and one locked temporal test.
Leakage, negative-control, shuffled-label, split-boundary, estimator-window, saturation, and clipping checks.
tests_verified: The in-memory observation passed jsonschema validation against observation.schema.json.
Constant-series sanity case produced persistence MAE 0.0.
Mean drift beat persistence on MAE in all three original validation folds; its mean validation MAE was 1.1367 versus 1.2488, an 8.98% reduction, and mean RMSE was 1.7680 versus 1.9720.
Selected mean-drift test predictions [88.920, 91.381, 91.723, 91.102] produced MAE 0.9430 and RMSE 1.1235; persistence test MAE/RMSE was 1.0212/1.3225.
A target_proxy predictor produced validation MAE 0.0, confirming why it is leakage rather than credible performance.
Twenty fixed-seed shuffled-target fits on the last validation fold had mean MAE 22.7217, range 19.2717-27.6685.
Noise-only ridge validation mean MAE was 15.8081, materially worse than baseline.
uncertainties: The sample and test are very small; four test errors do not support a precise generalization estimate.
No target unit, decision cost, forecast acceptance threshold, or deployment latency constraint was provided.
The synthetic invalid date strings prevent calendar-spacing or seasonality claims.
The late regime has only 16 rows and is only knowable after close, so future regime behavior is uncertain.
Feature saturation and missingness mechanisms are described but not statistically identifiable from this sample.
Adjacent one-step errors and overlapping training prefixes are dependent; folds are repeated temporal evidence, not independent replications.
validation: Original-fold mean drift MAE/RMSE by fold: 0.8234/1.0800, 1.8079/3.3950, 0.7790/0.8290.
Test was consulted only after selecting mean drift from validation.
The second fold spans the early-to-late change and is the hardest fold for both baseline and winner, indicating regime-shift risk.
